analysis:
This PR is a desktop-app renderer change: it ranks "Recommended for your Mac" models by per-chip 24h earnings from /v1/stats model_earnings[].by_chip. The content is wholly UI/data-presentation logic and a changelog entry. It does not touch the provider process, WebSocket, attestation, key custody, encryption, prefix cache, or fan helper, so TB-002/003/007/009/010/011/012/013 and the T-041 cache threat are unaffected.

Examined recommendations.ts (head lines 31-102). chipEarnings validates untrusted coordinator-supplied data: it reuses networkEarnings (freshness within 5 minutes, window 7d, id uniqueness), requires by_chip_window to be '24h', and checks that each entry has a string chip, a safe-integer machines count >= 1, and digit-only amount strings before calling BigInt. Malformed data yields null and falls back to network totals, so there is no exception path from BigInt on non-numeric input. Values are only rendered through React text interpolation (no dangerouslySetInnerHTML), so a malicious or compromised coordinator string such as the chip name cannot inject markup. The chip name is only compared to snapshot.machine.chip and printed in the subtitle.

recommendedModels with perChip uses perChip.get(a.id)! after filtering on mean > 0, so the non-null assertion is safe. chipRanking checks that the ranking is non-empty before the per-chip path is used, so the copy and the ranking fall back together. A residual integrity point: the coordinator could skew earnings figures to steer a user toward particular models. The coordinator is a trusted party, and the output is advisory and requires explicit user action. The Autopilot start action selects models only from the eligible local model list, and the existing recommendedStart is unchanged. Earnings displays use the existing money() helper.

No new IPC, filesystem, or network surface was added. The contracts.ts changes are type-only. I found no security regression and no required threat-model update. The only uncertainty is the coordinator side of by_chip publishing, which is platform-owned and outside the supplied evidence.
